title: Best app I’ve found for organization

This app lets me schedule everything with as much precision and detail as I want. If I were still working, I would easily be able to separate my work tasks from my home tasks.  I started out with the free version for quite a while, but then found that I liked it so well that some of the things in the pro version were going to be a large benefit as far as categorizing my tasks go. I don’t have it completely dialed in yet, but every time I dial it in a little further it just keeps getting better and better.  I would’ve loved to have had this when I was still working and had my own business. The deadline feature keeps me from continually putting off tasks that I tend to procrastinate on.  That is very helpful now and would’ve been really helpful when I was working.  And it’s a good thing this didn’t exist when I had children at home  because I would’ve been assigning them things left and right!  😄😄

title: Powerful Task Tool
body: I cannot do life without this tool. It takes a bit to get used to all the options and how to set it up best, but once it’s set up to fit your life, this powerful tool is a game changer to keeping me on task and allows me the head space to be fully focused with others when I’m not completing tasks. The daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly reminders are perfect for things I do regularly and don’t want to try to remember when I did it last. The import from a spreadsheet is perfect for my grad classes to easily copy and paste from the syllabus and import the tasks into Todoist. The different ways to view the task lists are flexible depending on my needs for that list. I love that I can set something to remind me every few days to do something and with the additional paid for features, I can keep on top of everything even more granularly. It is the perfect tool and I have not come across anything I’ve wanted to do that it cannot do. Their help section on their website is fantastic for figuring out how to do various things, no matter what I dream up. I used the free version for a while, which worked great, but about 6 months in, I realized the paid for version was worth it for the additional projects and for the deadline so I could have various school projects show up daily before the deadline and I could still remember when it HAD to be turned in. Get it - you won’t regret it. The best task tool I have ever found and it keeps me sane.
developer_response: Thank you so much for the incredibly thoughtful review, Laura 🤗️ It means a lot to hear how Todoist supports everything from your grad classes and recurring routines to giving you more headspace to focus on the people around you. We’re especially glad the flexibility, reminders, spreadsheet imports, deadlines, and Help Center have all been useful along the way. Thank you for making Todoist such a meaningful part of your life! ❤️

title: Bring Back Swipe Left

developer_response:
We're really sorry this change has been frustrating. We know swipe-to-select was part of many people’s muscle memory, and losing that can make the app feel worse rather than better at first. We didn’t remove it lightly. The previous swipe-to-select was a custom gesture that could conflict with iOS system gestures, which sometimes caused selections to fail or be cancelled unexpectedly. Unfortunately, we couldn’t make that behavior fully reliable. To avoid those issues and provide a more consistent experience, we moved to Apple’s native multi-select gestures.
We understand that this kind of change is disruptive, and we truly appreciate your patience and feedback as you adjust. You can still select multiple tasks using any of these methods:
• Tap the three dots in the top-right corner → Select tasks, then tap the tasks you want
• Use a two-finger swipe to enter selection mode (a standard iOS gesture)
• Press and hold a task → tap Select, then tap other tasks to add them to your selection

title: No longer supporting older iOS and shutting down!
body: I’ve been paid a user of this app for years. It’s helped me manage my cognitive needs as a part of my disability. Some of the updates to this app have made it less accessible and when I’ve reached out, I’ve never gotten a response. Now, the developers/management have decided to no longer support devices below iOS 17 and they are shutting my version down. My devices STILL work and I cannot afford to buy new things. These business decisions are made because the bottom line matters more than access and people with special needs do not matter. That is a horrible thing to experience. I can’t express my disappointment to loose access (and the energy I’ll need to use to learn something new) when this app stops working across my devices if I don’t spend money to get new stuff. AND the browser isn’t supported on a mobile device when they shut down the app! Their response to my “no longer supported device is that I can use it on my other devices. For the well-healed crowd apparently! And they just charged me for another year and none of my devices work!
developer_response: We’re really sorry for the frustration this has caused 💔 Unfortunately, we can’t continue supporting older iOS versions, as Todoist relies on newer system updates for stability and security. If this affects your renewal, our support team is happy to help. Please reach out via the contact form: https://todoist.com/contact

title: Not for Mobile Phone Users
body:
And purchase this app, as it was highly recommended by AI. Although this it has some nice features, it is designed primarily for desktop and businesses, not individual mobile phone users. 1) you were unable to easily sort your task by context such as phone errands, etc. compare this to Apple reminders she’s basically a one and done. I updated the app just now to see if some of the issues were resolved, and they were not. In fact, they were worse. Sort by contacts, which is foundational to the clarify step in GTD, go to browse, select filters, choose one filter  (if you choose more than one, it won’t even sort at all), go back to inbox, and you’ll see just the items in the context/filter you chose. The new update changed this so that it’s even less convenient for mobile users. 2) lack of easily accessible Health Center for mobile users when browsing for a help help topic. The mobile app did take you to YouTube. The YouTube videos show you how to use the feature you’re searching on the desktop version. If you’re lucky, there’ll be a small section at how to use a feature for your phone.
I could go on, but hopefully you get the idea. It’s really quite pitiful.

title: Cheers from a dedicated fan!!!
body: First, let me say that I admit to being a bit picky in how I do things. My wife would call it something else, but that’s for another time. I’ve been using Todoist now for 4 years, and I could not be more pleased with it. In fact, I’ve become so much an advocate I regularly have requests from other people to show them what it is and how I use it, and then help them set it up for themselves!! The flexible and multiple means to organize everything — Projects, Sections, Folders, Tasks, Sub-tasks — makes it easier to organize and re-organize things that I simply haven’t seen in other apps. Add to that the labeling and filtering capabilities, and Todoist just can’t be beat. If you’re a busy executive or entrepreneur then Todoist is the only app I would recommend for you.
developer_response: It is wonderful to hear that we have supported your GTD workflow for four years! We are honored that you advocate for us and help others set up their systems. title: Project filtering drives me crazy
body:
I love this app in so many ways, but there is one seemingly minor missing feature that just drives me crazy and actually deeply impacts my workflow and usage. My husband and I have a shared todo list. We both add items to the list, and sometimes we claim some of the items ahead of time but some items stay unassigned until one or the other of us gets to it first. It would be immensely helpful to be able to filter our shared project view by “assigned to me OR no one” but you simply can’t do this! Argh! As a software engineer myself, I know this would be relatively straightforward to implement. 

There are very customizable filter views, but they are separate from the project and don’t preserve the section organization/grouping from the project. 

So until they add this little feature or I give up on this app, I’m stuck scrolling through all those things my husband is supposed to be (eventually) getting around to
developer_response:
We understand how frustrating the project filtering limitation can be, especially for shared lists! If you haven’t already, please try using this filter query:`!assigned | assigned to: me`
This will display tasks that are either unassigned or assigned to you.
If you still need help, please reach out to our CX team at https://todoist.com/contact - they’ll be happy to look into it for you.

title: Is it poor quality control?
body:
Location based notifications don’t honor the recurring day and ALWAYS notify regardless of scheduled day/time. Even though I have a task set repeating weekly only on one day of the week with a location based reminder, I get notifications/reminders every single time I go to that location despite it not even showing in my today view nor being set for that day. That’s pretty wack. 

Also, I have not been able to turn off email notifications for tasks. I have email on my phone as well as Todoist. I don’t want two notifications for the same thing within minutes of each other. Let me turn off email notifications! I have ALL available email notifications turned off and I still get notifications for tasks in my email clogging up my inbox for no reason.

Please do better.

title: Probably Great for IBM employees
body:
The interface needs a lot of love. This is surely a very effective app with all of its whiz-bang features. But what really want is some interface that is fun. Confetti is tiny fun. But why is the text on my to-do list not adjustable? I use this on an iPad mini and in my dream the interface is skeuomorphic as a clipboard with a page on it. But at least let me pick different fonts. At at the very very least different font SIZES. If you want me to check this first thing in the morning you should give me the ability to see it without my glasses on. And let me add things before I go to sleep. 

Put another way:you probably could make this a more boing app, but I have no idea how. 

TBH even your confetti is weak. Tiny. Go wild! Make it reactive the accelerometer so it always falls down. 

When your app is literally every coding 101 project you gotta do more.  Sure you link with corporate accounts and tasks for 600 employees blah blah blah. 

Hire a UI person. A fun one. Let them go wild. Then hide all of their work in the “View” menu so your suits don’t ever find it.

title: Part of my daily life

I love the ease of adding tasks and by using symbols and times, have those tasks in the correct project with due dates and reminders. 

The team has really enhanced the software over this time adding more and more functionality. 

My only complaint about the application, and it’s a big one for me, is the syncing. Very often when I mark tasks off on my computer, they are not marked complete on my phone. I’ve tried suggestions from support and often it doesn’t work. 

If you are looking at a repeatable task, and mark it complete twice by accident, it will complete for the next day too. That has thrown me off more than once. For example, I mark a task complete on my computer and later see the task not complete on my phone (not yet synced), then mark it complete on my phone, that reoccurring task will be marked complete for the next iteration even though what is shown on my phone was today’s task. There has to be a better way to index the tasks. 

Regardless, I really like this app and suggest to others to whom I think it is a good fit.

I have used this for a couple years and it seemed to work well. This is a big problem - not able to see and therefore not working on tasks, let alone a loss of faith in the product.  Missing tasks ranged from ones created recently to ones not touched for over a year.

Todoist phone did show a sync had happened seconds before (with the tasks showing).

 It took several business days to get a canned reply (eg were they marked completed?), I redirected them to look at the info I originally sent.
Another business day and I was told to log off and log on but first gather info on all phone tasks that were not properly synced or data could be list.  No way to do this with software (eg a backup of phone tasks).  I have thousands of tasks, even if only 100, it is unreasonable to ask this of a user.  Todoist needs debugging  software to determine which tasks were not properly synced.
Support is not at the level it was when I first started. And despite me paying for the product trouble tickets are the only contact with the company. 

I requested a way to prevent sync problems and a way to confirm phone tasks info was not lost.  I don’t expect thru will do either task.

It is unreasonable to ask a user to log off and lot on regularly in case sync is not working, each time spending ton of time to confirm all phone tasks are correctly updated on the webpage.

A severe bug that really undermines  the trust in the application, I am off to review other task apps as I need a reliable one.

title: Getting there
body: It works for me if I do some prep before making my lists. I wish there was a way to see all the days of the month at once and that it had year view as well from which I can navigate to certain months and days. It really helps me to plan out my day and month if I can get a visual of it. Also, the recurring tasks feature needs some work. Sometimes I want to skip a task for that week or day and there’s no way to skip a recurring task. I have to mark it as done because if I delete it, then I’m deleting the recurring task completely.
developer_response: Thanks for the feedback! Good news—on the Pro plan, there’s a monthly calendar view and the option to postpone recurring tasks without marking them as done. Let us know if you’d like any help exploring these features! 😊

body: Todoist is a to do list app that you can adapt to your particular situation. it can sync to all of your different devices. It’s graphics or pleasant and simple. title: To much control of your device
body: I thought this would work for me, but like a lot of apps to get what they say it does it costs you money even for short trial. When went to remove it. It stayed on my calendar no matter what I did to delete it. Todoist’s own instructions for removing the app and its attachments to everything didn’t work. Thankfully Google had a solution in the calendar settings online.   Buyer beware!!!
developer_response: We’re sorry for the trouble with removing Todoist from your calendar. We understand how frustrating this can be and appreciate your feedback. Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you need more help!

title: Good but soo limited
body: The most basic thing, adding tasks is limited to 300 "active" tasks even with premium. This is ridiculous. I wanted to use this app for all of my needs and frankly I do a lot and have a lot to do. If I break things down the way that works best for me, I end up with way over 300 tasks and I like to use this as a brain dump. However, I'm going to have to find another app than can handle reality. Makes no sense that there would be these limitations. If we use this for work and we use this for home, and if we're parents, and if we have social lives... 300? Seriously? That may sound like lot, but if you break down your tasks (including grocery lists) you will likely get to the thousands. No one works on one project (which can have 300 tasks - long and short term ~ in itself. Please expand this. Until then, I'lll be on a search for an app that can handle reality and once I find it, I'lll cancel my premium subscription. Apple notes can handle more... I prefer a simpler list, though, for these task items ~
developer_response: We’re sorry to hear that you find the 300 limit too low. We’ve shared your feedback with the team. If you have any other feature requests, please feel free to share them through this form: https://tally.so/r/3jB98J
